obligations.statement: Management ensures the quality management system meets its intended objectives and measures how it is managed and how it performs in areas such as self-inspections, inspections, quality and supplier audits; complaints, returns and recalls; changes and deviations; rejected batches; quality control, OOS and OOT results; maintenance; qualification and validation; CAPA; and risk management.
obligations.quote: Management should ensure that the quality management system achieves its intended objectives and measures managing and performance in areas such as: ■ self-inspections, inspections, quality audits and supplier’s audits ■ complaints, returns and recalls ■ changes and deviations ■ rejected batches ■ quality control, out-of-specification results and out-of-trend results ■ maintenance ■ qualification and validation ■ corrective and preventive actions ■ risk management.

obligations.statement: Written SOPs and programmes exist for periodic self-inspections, quality audits and supplier audits.
obligations.quote: There should be written standard operating procedures and programmes for periodic self-inspections, quality audits and supplier audits.

obligations.statement: Self-inspections are carried out routinely, following a self-inspection programme.
obligations.quote: Self-inspections should be performed routinely in accordance with a self- inspection programme.

obligations.statement: The self-inspection team is made up of staff with suitable knowledge and experience.
obligations.quote: The team responsible for self-inspection should consist of personnel with the appropriate knowledge and experience.

obligations.statement: Self-inspection team members can be drawn from inside or outside the manufacturer.
obligations.quote: Team members may be from inside or outside the manufacturer

obligations.statement: Self-inspection team members are free from bias.
obligations.quote: members of the team should be free from bias.

obligations.statement: Self-inspections can cover areas such as premises, personnel, equipment, maintenance and calibration, storage conditions of materials and finished products, production and in-process controls, quality control, documentation and data integrity, change control and deviations, complaints and recalls, qualification and validation, and cleaning procedures.
obligations.quote: Areas to be covered in self-inspections may include: ■ premises ■ personnel ■ equipment ■ maintenance and calibration ■ storage conditions of materials and finished products ■ production and in-process controls ■ quality control ■ documentation, data generation and data integrity ■ change control and deviations management ■ complaints and recalls ■ qualification and validation ■ cleaning procedures.

obligations.statement: When inspecting an excipient manufacturer, the intended end use of the excipient is taken into account, in particular whether it will be used to prepare a sterile dosage form.
obligations.quote: The excipient’s end use should be considered during inspection of excipient manufacturers. It is particularly important to know whether the excipient will be used in the preparation of a sterile dosage form.

obligations.statement: Where the excipient manufacturer claims in specifications, labels or a drug master file that an excipient is pyrogen free, the manufacturer ensures that it is.
obligations.quote: The excipient manufacturer is responsible for ensuring that excipients are pyrogen free if the manufacturer makes such a representation in specifications, labels or a drug master file.

obligations.statement: SOPs and related records are available covering at minimum: equipment; analytical apparatus and instruments; OOS results; maintenance and calibration; cleaning and sanitization; personnel matters such as training, clothing and hygiene; qualification and validation; self-inspection and audits; complaints; recalls; and returns.
obligations.quote: Standard operating procedures and associated records should be available for at least the following: ■ equipment ■ analytical apparatus and instruments ■ out-of-specification results ■ maintenance and calibration ■ cleaning and sanitization ■ personnel matters, such as training, clothing and hygiene ■ qualification and validation ■ self-inspection and audits ■ complaints ■ recalls ■ returns.

obligations.statement: The manufacturer puts in place measures for continual improvement of the quality management system, of manufacturing and testing procedures, and of product quality.
obligations.quote: Manufacturers should implement measures to continuously improve the quality management system, manufacturing and testing procedures, and the quality of their products.

obligations.statement: Improvement measures can include reviewing root causes of nonconformances, complaint investigations and their outcomes, and results of self-inspections, audits and other trends.
obligations.quote: These measures may include the review of root causes of nonconformances, quality complaint investigations and outcomes, and results from self-inspections, audits and other trends.

obligations.statement: Self-inspections are carried out routinely.
obligations.quote: Self-inspections should be performed routinely

obligations.statement: Additional self-inspections can be carried out on special occasions, for example after product recalls or repeated rejections, or when a health authority inspection is announced.
obligations.quote: may be, in addition, performed on special occasions, e.g. in the case of product recalls or repeated rejections, or when an inspection by the health authorities is announced

obligations.statement: The self-inspection team is made up of people able to assess GMP implementation objectively.
obligations.quote: The team responsible for self-inspection should consist of personnel who can evaluate the implementation of GMP objectively

obligations.statement: All recommended corrective actions from self-inspection are implemented.
obligations.quote: all recommenda- tions for corrective action should be implemented

obligations.statement: The self-inspection procedure is documented.
obligations.quote: The procedure for self-inspection should be documented

obligations.statement: An effective follow-up programme for self-inspections is in place.
obligations.quote: there should be an effec- tive follow-up programme

obligations.statement: Written self-inspection instructions are established that set a minimum, uniform standard of requirements.
obligations.quote: Written instructions for self-inspection should be established to provide a minimum and uniform standard of requirements.

obligations.statement: Self-inspection instructions can include GMP questionnaires covering at least: personnel; premises including personnel facilities; maintenance of buildings and equipment; storage of starting materials and finished products; equipment; production and in-process controls; quality control; documentation; sanitation and hygiene; validation and revalidation programmes; calibration of instruments or measurement systems; recall procedures; complaints management; labels control; and results of earlier self-inspections and corrective steps taken.
obligations.quote: These may include questionnaires on GMP requirements covering at least the following items: (a) personnel (b) premises including personnel facilities (c) maintenance of buildings and equipment (d) storage of starting materials and finished products (e) equipment (f) production and in-process controls (g) quality control (h) documentation (i) sanitation and hygiene (j) validation and revalidation programmes (k) calibration of instruments or measurements systems (l) recall procedures (m) complaints management (n) labels control (o) results of previous self-inspections and any corrective steps taken.

obligations.statement: Management appoints a self-inspection team of local staff who are experts in their own fields and familiar with GMP.
obligations.quote: Management should appoint a self-inspection team from local staff who are expert in their own fields and familiar with GMP.

obligations.statement: Self-inspection team members can be appointed from inside or outside the company.
obligations.quote: The members of the team may be appointed from inside or outside the company.

obligations.statement: The site can set how often self-inspections are done according to company requirements.
obligations.quote: The frequency at which self-inspections are conducted may de- pend on company requirements.

obligations.statement: A report is prepared when each self-inspection is completed.
obligations.quote: A report should be made at the completion of a self-inspection.

obligations.statement: The self-inspection report contains the results, the evaluation and conclusions, and the recommended corrective actions.
obligations.quote: The report should include: (a) self-inspection results (b) evaluation and conclusions (c) recommended corrective actions.

obligations.statement: Company management evaluates the self-inspection report and the corrective actions, as necessary.
obligations.quote: The company management should evaluate both the self- inspection report and the corrective actions as necessary.

obligations.statement: The site can supplement self-inspections with a quality audit.
obligations.quote: It may be useful to supplement self-inspections with a quality audit.

obligations.statement: Quality audits can be extended to suppliers and contractors.
obligations.quote: Such audits may also be extended to suppliers and contractors.

obligations.statement: The main responsibilities of the independent quality unit(s) are not delegated.
obligations.quote: The main responsibilities of the independent quality unit(s) should not be delegated.

obligations.statement: The quality unit's responsibilities are described in writing.
obligations.quote: These responsibilities should be described in writing

obligations.statement: The quality unit releases or rejects every API.
obligations.quote: Releasing or rejecting all APIs.

obligations.statement: The quality unit releases or rejects intermediates that will be used outside the manufacturing company's control.
obligations.quote: Releasing or rejecting intermediates for use outside the control of the manufacturing company.

obligations.statement: The quality unit sets up a system for releasing or rejecting raw materials, intermediates, and packaging and labelling materials.
obligations.quote: Establishing a system to release or reject raw materials, intermediates, packaging and labelling materials.

obligations.statement: The quality unit reviews completed batch production and laboratory control records for critical process steps before the API is released for distribution.
obligations.quote: Reviewing completed batch production and laboratory control records of critical process steps before release of the API for distribution.

obligations.statement: The quality unit makes sure critical deviations are investigated and resolved.
obligations.quote: Making sure that critical deviations are investigated and resolved.

obligations.statement: The quality unit approves all specifications and master production instructions.
obligations.quote: Approving all speciﬁcations and master production instructions.

obligations.statement: The quality unit approves every procedure that affects the quality of intermediates or APIs.
obligations.quote: Approving all procedures impacting the quality of intermediates or APIs.

obligations.statement: The quality unit makes sure internal audits (self-inspections) are carried out.
obligations.quote: Making sure that internal audits (self-inspections) are performed.

obligations.statement: The quality unit approves contract manufacturers of intermediates and APIs.
obligations.quote: Approving intermediate and API contract manufacturers.

obligations.statement: The quality unit approves changes that could affect the quality of intermediates or APIs.
obligations.quote: Approving changes that potentially impact quality of intermediates or APIs.

obligations.statement: The quality unit reviews and approves validation protocols and reports.
obligations.quote: Reviewing and approving validation protocols and reports.

obligations.statement: The quality unit makes sure quality-related complaints are investigated and resolved.
obligations.quote: Making sure that quality-related complaints are investigated and resolved.

obligations.statement: The quality unit makes sure effective systems are used to maintain and calibrate critical equipment.
obligations.quote: Making sure that effective systems are used for maintaining and calibrating critical equipment.

obligations.statement: The quality unit makes sure materials are properly tested and results are reported.
obligations.quote: Making sure that materials are appropriately tested and the results are reported.

obligations.statement: Where appropriate, the quality unit makes sure stability data exist to support retest or expiry dates and storage conditions for APIs and/or intermediates.
obligations.quote: Making sure that there are stability data to support retest or expiry dates and storage conditions on APIs and/or intermediates where appropriate.

obligations.statement: The quality unit performs product quality reviews as defined in section 2.5.
obligations.quote: Performing product quality reviews (as deﬁned in section 2.5).

obligations.statement: Audit findings and corrective actions are documented and reported to the firm's responsible management.
obligations.quote: Audit ﬁndings and corrective actions should be documented and brought to the attention of the responsible management of the ﬁrm.

obligations.statement: Agreed corrective actions are completed in a timely and effective way.
obligations.quote: Agreed corrective actions should be completed in a timely and effective manner.

obligations.statement: The PQS ensures product realization through a system that is designed, qualified, planned, implemented, maintained and continually improved so products with appropriate quality attributes are delivered consistently.
obligations.quote: product realization is achieved by designing, qualifying, planning, implementing, maintaining and continuously improving a system that allows the consistent delivery of products with appropriate quality attributes

obligations.statement: The PQS ensures product and process knowledge is managed across all life-cycle stages.
obligations.quote: product and process knowledge is managed throughout all life- cycle stages

obligations.statement: The PQS ensures products are designed and developed taking account of GMP and related codes such as GLP and GCP.
obligations.quote: pharmaceutical products are designed and developed in a way that takes account of the requirements of GMP and other associated codes such as those of good laboratory practice (GLP) and good clinical practice (GCP)

obligations.statement: The PQS ensures production and control operations are clearly specified in writing and GMP requirements are adopted.
obligations.quote: production and control operations are clearly specified in a written form and GMP requirements are adopted

obligations.statement: The PQS ensures managerial responsibilities are clearly set out in job descriptions.
obligations.quote: managerial responsibilities are clearly specified in job descriptions

obligations.statement: The PQS ensures arrangements exist for making, supplying and using the correct starting and packaging materials, for selecting and monitoring suppliers, and for verifying that each delivery is the correct material from the approved supply chain.
obligations.quote: arrangements are made for the manufacture, supply and use of the correct starting and packaging materials, the selection and monitoring of suppliers and for verifying that each delivery is the correct material from the approved supply chain

obligations.statement: The PQS ensures all necessary controls on starting materials, intermediates and bulk products, plus other in-process controls, calibrations and validations, are carried out.
obligations.quote: all necessary controls on starting materials, intermediate products, and bulk products and other in-process controls, calibrations and validations are carried out

obligations.statement: The PQS ensures the finished product is correctly processed and checked following defined procedures.
obligations.quote: the finished product is correctly processed and checked, according to the defined procedures

obligations.statement: The PQS ensures no product is sold or supplied until the authorized persons (see sections 9.11 and 9.12) have certified that each batch was produced and controlled in line with the marketing authorization and any other regulations on production, control and release.
obligations.quote: pharmaceutical products are not sold or supplied before the authorized persons (see also sections 9.11 and 9.12) have certified that each production batch has been produced and controlled in accordance with the requirements of the marketing authorization and any other regulations relevant to the production, control and release of pharmaceutical products

obligations.statement: The PQS ensures processes exist to manage outsourced activities.
obligations.quote: processes are in place to assure the management of outsourced activities

obligations.statement: The PQS ensures adequate arrangements exist so that, as far as possible, products are stored, distributed and handled in a way that keeps their quality throughout shelf-life.
obligations.quote: satisfactory arrangements exist to ensure, as far as possible, that the pharmaceutical products are stored, distributed and subsequently handled so that quality is maintained throughout their shelf-life

obligations.statement: The PQS ensures a self-inspection and/or quality audit procedure exists that regularly assesses how effective and applicable the PQS is.
obligations.quote: there is a procedure for self-inspection and/or quality audit that regularly appraises the effectiveness and applicability of the PQS

obligations.statement: The PQS ensures products and processes are monitored and the results are used in batch release, in deviation investigations, and to take preventive action against future deviations.
obligations.quote: product and processes are monitored and the results taken into account in batch release, in the investigation of deviations and, with a view to taking preventive action to avoid potential deviations occurring in the future

obligations.statement: The PQS ensures planned changes are evaluated and approved in advance, before implementation, taking regulatory notification and approval into account where required.
obligations.quote: arrangements are in place for the prospective evaluation and approval of planned changes and their approval prior to implementation taking into account regulatory notification and approval where required

obligations.statement: The PQS ensures that after any change is implemented, an evaluation confirms the quality objectives were met and product quality was not unintentionally harmed.
obligations.quote: After implementation of any change, an evaluation is undertaken to confirm that the quality objectives were achieved and that there was no unintended adverse impact on product quality

obligations.statement: The PQS ensures regular product quality reviews are carried out to verify process consistency and identify where improvement is needed.
obligations.quote: regular reviews of the quality of pharmaceutical products are conducted with the objective of verifying the consistency of the process and identifying where there is a need for improvement

obligations.statement: The PQS ensures a state of control is established and kept through effective monitoring and control systems for process performance and product quality.
obligations.quote: a state of control is established and maintained by developing and using effective monitoring and control systems for process performance and product quality

obligations.statement: The PQS ensures continual improvement is supported by implementing quality improvements suited to current process and product knowledge.
obligations.quote: continual improvement is facilitated through the implementation of quality improvements appropriate to the current level of process and product knowledge

obligations.statement: The PQS ensures a quality risk management system exists.
obligations.quote: there is a system for QRM

obligations.statement: The PQS ensures deviations, suspected product defects and other problems are reported, investigated and recorded.
obligations.quote: deviations, suspected product defects and other problems are reported, investigated and recorded

obligations.statement: A suitable level of root cause analysis is applied when investigating deviations, suspected defects and other problems.
obligations.quote: An appropriate level of root cause analysis is applied during such investigations.

obligations.statement: Investigations identify the most likely root cause(s), and suitable corrective and/or preventive actions (CAPAs) are identified and carried out.
obligations.quote: The most likely root cause(s) should be identified and appropriate corrective actions and/or preventive actions (CAPAs) should be identified and taken.

obligations.statement: The effectiveness of CAPAs is monitored.
obligations.quote: The effectiveness of CAPAs should be monitored.

obligations.statement: Regular, periodic or rolling quality reviews are carried out for every product, export-only products included, to verify process consistency and that current starting material and finished product specifications are still appropriate, to show trends and to identify product and process improvements.
obligations.quote: Regular, periodic or rolling quality reviews of all pharmaceutical products, including export-only products, should be conducted with the objective of verifying the consistency of the existing process and the appropriateness of current specifications for both starting materials and finished product, to highlight any trends and to identify product and process improvements.

obligations.statement: Product quality reviews are normally performed and documented annually, taking earlier reviews into account.
obligations.quote: Such reviews should normally be conducted and documented annually, taking into account previous reviews

obligations.statement: The quality review covers starting and packaging materials used, especially those from new sources, and in particular the supply chain traceability of active substances.
obligations.quote: review of starting materials and packaging materials used for the product, especially those from new sources and in particular the review of supply chain traceability of active substances

obligations.statement: The quality review covers critical in-process controls and finished product results.
obligations.quote: a review of critical in-process controls, and finished product results

obligations.statement: The quality review covers every batch that failed its specification(s) and the related investigation.

obligations.statement: The quality review covers all significant deviations or non-conformances, their investigations, and how effective the resulting CAPAs were.
obligations.quote: a review of all significant deviations or non-conformances, the related investigations and the effectiveness of resultant CAPAs taken

obligations.statement: The quality review covers all changes to processes or analytical methods.
obligations.quote: a review of all changes made to the processes or analytical methods

obligations.statement: The quality review covers dossier variations submitted, granted or refused.
obligations.quote: a review of dossier variations submitted, granted or refused

obligations.statement: The quality review covers stability monitoring programme results and any adverse trends.
obligations.quote: a review of the results of the stability monitoring programme and any adverse trends

obligations.statement: The quality review covers all quality-related returns, complaints and recalls and the investigations done at the time.
obligations.quote: a review of all quality-related returns, complaints and recalls and the investigations performed at the time

obligations.statement: The quality review covers whether any other earlier corrective actions on product processes or equipment were adequate.

obligations.statement: The quality review covers post-marketing commitments for new dossiers and dossier variations.
obligations.quote: post-marketing commitments for new dossiers and variations to the dossiers

obligations.statement: The quality review covers the qualification status of relevant equipment and utilities (for example HVAC, water or compressed gases) and the results of monitoring their output.
obligations.quote: the qualification status of relevant equipment and utilities, e.g. heating, ventilation and air-conditioning (HVAC), water or compressed gases and a review of the results of monitoring the output of such equipment and utilities

obligations.statement: The quality review covers technical agreements to confirm they are current.
obligations.quote: a review of technical agreements to ensure that they are up to date

obligations.statement: The manufacturer, and the marketing authorization holder where different, evaluate the review results and assess, within the PQS, whether CAPA or revalidation is needed.
obligations.quote: The manufacturer and, where different, marketing authorization holder, should evaluate the results of the review and an assessment should be made as to whether CAPA or any revalidation should be undertaken, under the PQS.

obligations.statement: CAPAs arising from the review are completed promptly and effectively following documented procedures.
obligations.quote: CAPAs should be completed in a timely and effective manner, according to documented procedures.

obligations.statement: Procedures exist for the ongoing management and review of these CAPAs.
obligations.quote: There should be procedures for the ongoing management and review of these actions

obligations.statement: Self-inspection verifies that the CAPA management and review procedures are effective.
obligations.quote: the effectiveness of these procedures should be verified during self-inspection

obligations.quote: Quality reviews may be grouped by product type, e.g. solid dosage forms, liquid dosage forms, or sterile products, where scientifically justified.

obligations.quote: Where the marketing authorization holder is not the manufacturer, there should be a technical agreement in place between the various parties that defines their respective responsibilities in producing the quality review.
